data.name: Janardan
data.gender_notes: Janardan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Janardan is derived from the Sanskrit language and is a combination of two words: ‘Jan’ which means ‘people’ and ‘Ardhan’ which means ‘lord’ or ‘ruler’. The name Janardan thus signifies ‘Lord of the People’. This name is given to a boy in the belief that he will rule over and protect his people. The name Janardan carries the meaning “Lord of the People” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Janardan usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the people and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of compassion and leadership, representing the divine ruler and protector of his people.
data.etymology: Janardan belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the People.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Janardan total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Janardan holds significant cultural importance in Hinduism, particularly in the region of Maharashtra, India. It is closely associated with Lord Vishnu, who is worshipped as Janardan, and is believed to be the advocate for the pleas of his devotees. The name evokes a sense of royalty and protection and is often used as a title of respect for an individual known for his leadership qualities.
data.spiritual_significance: Janardan is not only a name but also a symbol of God's love and protection for his people. The spiritual significance of the name emanates from the belief that the one who is the ruler of all, is also intimately connected to the smallest of beings. The name is a reminder of the Divine's unwavering grace and compassion towards his devotees. In essence, Janardan represents the ultimate expression of God as the visible protector and the invisible source.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Janardan symbolizes the omnipotent and merciful form of Lord Vishnu, who is capable of relieving all forms of suffering and sorrow. The name 'Janardan' is derived from 'Janani' (mother) and 'ardhan' (whose heart is filled with all emotions) - reflecting the nurturing and compassionate nature of the deity.

vedic_reference.note: Janardan is a popular name in Hinduism, and is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Janardana', which means 'God of the People' or 'Lord of the People'. It is also one of the many names of Lord Vishnu. The name is mentioned in various Hindu scriptures and mythologies, including the Mahabharata and the Bhagavad Gita.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Janardan is mentioned in the Mahabharata as a name of Lord Krishna The name Janardan carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
